extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A new texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using an extensible methodology for high-quality, diverse texture images via text-to-image models.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak, Patrick McDaniel
extraction.citeAs: Hoak, B., & McDaniel, P. (2025). On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by generating texture images using text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion) based on constructed prompts. The process involved generating prompts with specific descriptors, generating images, and applying a three-stage refinement process (frequency analysis, patch variance filtering, and CLIP scoring) to filter out low-quality or non-texture images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text prompts constructed from combinations of texture classes, artistic descriptors, spatial descriptors, color enhancers, and colors. The raw data source for the underlying model is Stable Diffusion.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied: (1) Frequency filtering to remove object-like images by retaining top 80% of images with highest frequency cutoff values; (2) Patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by removing bottom 20% of images with lowest mean patch variance; (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure prompt alignment by removing bottom 20% of images with lowest CLIP scores.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were generated using Stable Diffusion. Flagged images (NSFW) were excluded. A three-stage refinement process was applied: frequency filtering, patch variance filtering, and CLIP score filtering to ensure quality, diversity, and prompt alignment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was conducted to assess quality and representativeness. 9 participants rated 100 images each on a scale of 1 to 5 for overall quality and how well the image represented the provided descriptor.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation scores were compared against CLIP scores to validate alignment. Results showed that CLIP scores effectively represent human scores for alignment between prompts and images. Human evaluators favored textures that were less homogeneous and structured.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion, CLIP, Inception model, Fourier transforms
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to aid in understanding high-level features models learn, uncovering biases (specifically texture bias), and identifying security vulnerabilities. It supports research in interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits biases related to the NSFW safety filter of Stable Diffusion, which flagged up to 60% of generated images as NSFW despite benign prompts. Certain texture descriptors (e.g., 'paisley') triggered high flagging rates. Additionally, some texture classes (e.g., 'grid', 'polka-dotted') had worse quality scores compared to others (e.g., 'hairy', 'flaky').
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is synthetic and may not perfectly replicate real-world textures. The generation process was affected by the NSFW safety filter, requiring exclusion of flagged images. Some structured textures performed worse in quality metrics. The dataset is limited to 2D textures.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Specifically for texture-based tasks, measuring texture bias, understanding model features, and constructing texture-object associations.
